log: |rule|Species Clause: Limit one of each Pokémon

decisions.thought:
Lead: 49% BRING: dragapult, 21% BRING: whimsicott, 9% BRING: gholdengo
Pick 2: 27% BRING: chandelure, 26% BRING: palafin, 18% BRING: whimsicott
Pick 3: 36% BRING: palafin, 26% BRING: toxapex, 24% BRING: whimsicott

Team plan: Incineroar leads for Intimidate, Fake Out and Parting Shot. Garchomp (Mega) is the main physical sweeper, and Kingambit handles Ghost/Fire types like Chandelure and Dragapult. Watch Dragapult's speed and Gholdengo's special damage. Toxapex is a physical wall, so Earthquake is the answer to it.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I need to choose 3 from my team against the opponent's lineup of gholdengo, palafin, dragapult, toxapex, chandelure, and whimsicott. I'm weighing the main threats—dragapult's speed, gholdengo and chandelure's special attacks, and toxapex's wall potential—and thinking about which of my attackers like Garchomp could punch through toxapex with Earthquake.

I'm leaning toward Incineroar for intimidate and support, Garchomp for raw power, and either Gholdengo or Kingambit for coverage. Kingambit's Dark-typing hits Chandelure super effectively, while Gholdengo's Steel typing gives good neutral coverage against most of their team, though it's weak against Whimsicott's Fairy typing.

decisions.thought: 81% MOVE: dragonpulse, 8% SWITCH: chandelure, 6% SWITCH: palafin

Turn 1: Dragapult (Dragon/Ghost, possibly Infiltrator or Clear Body) is already at -1 Atk. Fake Out does nothing to it (Ghost is immune to Normal). Flare Blitz is resisted by its Dragon typing. Parting Shot is super effective (Dark vs Ghost) and cuts Atk and SpA, so I'm using it to pivot out. Next: bring in Garchomp (faster, Earthquake/Stone Edge) or Kingambit, which can handle Dragapult. Opponent team: Gholdengo, Palafin, Toxapex, Chandelure, Whimsicott. Toxapex needs Earthquake.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Right, Dragapult's Ghost typing makes it immune to Fake Out, so that attack does nothing here. Flare Blitz would also be resisted since Fire is weak against Dragon.

I'm weighing other options: Parting Shot would drop its stats before switching, potentially bringing in something like Garchomp or Kingambit for a more favorable matchup against the Dragon/Ghost typing, though I need to check how each of those would actually fare against Dragapult's likely moves.

decisions.thought: Dragapult is at -2 Atk and -1 SpA after Parting Shot and Intimidate, so its physical attack is weakened. Kingambit's Dark moves hit Dragapult's Ghost typing super effectively, and Dragon Pulse is only neutral against Kingambit. Kingambit is slower than Dragapult, so Sucker Punch is the priority option if Dragapult attacks. Garchomp (Mega) is the main threat later, and Earthquake is the answer to Toxapex. Gholdengo and Chandelure have strong special attacks, so keep Incineroar's Intimidate in mind when they switch in.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm checking the speed comparison between Garchomp and Dragapult, then working out Kingambit's Dark-type Kowtow Cleave effectiveness against Dragapult's Dragon/Ghost typing—super effective against the Ghost part, neutral against Dragon.

Dragapult likely outspeeds Garchomp and its Dragon Pulse hits for 2x, though Kingambit only takes neutral damage from it since Steel doesn't resist Dragon, and Kingambit's physical bulk helps it tank that hit while Dragapult's SpA is lowered.

Dark hits Dragapult super effectively, and Sucker Punch gives Kingambit priority if Dragapult attacks first, making it the better answer despite being slower. I'll go with Kingambit.

decisions.thought: 52% SWITCH: chandelure, 38% SWITCH: palafin, 10% MOVE: dragonpulse

Turn 2: Dragapult (Dragon/Ghost) is at -2 Atk and -1 SpA after Parting Shot and Intimidate. It outspeeds Kingambit. Dragapult's revealed move is Dragon Pulse, which is neutral on Kingambit. Kingambit's Dark moves are super effective on Dragapult. Kowtow Cleave doesn't check accuracy and should KO. Garchomp (Mega) answers Toxapex with Earthquake. Gholdengo and Chandelure have strong specials; Intimidate helps when they switch in.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave hits Dragapult for solid Dark damage boosted by Black Glasses and the Ghost weakness, but since Dragapult's Atk is lowered and this is calculated as physical damage from Kingambit's side, I need to check whether Dragapult's own stat drop even factors in here since it's the attacker's stats that matter, not the target's.

decisions.thought: 97% MOVE: closecombat, 1% SWITCH: dragapult, 1% MOVE: waterfall

Palafin (Zero to Hero, pure Water) outspeeds Kingambit. Water is resisted by Kingambit's Steel typing, so Palafin's attacks should do little. Dragapult is at -2 Atk and -1 SpA, and Kowtow Cleave already KO'd Chandelure. Plan: Swords Dance while Kingambit tanks Palafin's water attacks, then sweep. Incineroar (low HP) and Garchomp (Earthquake for Toxapex) stay in reserve. Sucker Punch is risky if the target isn't attacking.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm noting that Palafin's Water typing only hits Kingambit for half damage since Water is neutral against Dark and resisted by Steel, so its Hero form moves like Jet Punch or Wave Crash won't be especially threatening to it.

Kowtow Cleave from Kingambit also hits Palafin neutrally and does solid damage given its decent BP and Black Glasses boost, though Palafin's superior speed lets it act first. I'm also weighing whether Ice Punch could change this matchup, checking Ice's effectiveness against Kingambit's Dark/Steel typing.

Given Kingambit resists Palafin's Water-type attacks, I'll lean toward Swords Dance to set up for a sweep rather than attacking immediately.

decisions.thought: Kingambit fell to Palafin's Close Combat. Palafin (Life Orb, Zero to Hero, pure Water) is at 90%. Dragapult is still around, with Atk and SpA lowered by Parting Shot and Intimidate. Garchomp is my healthy, fast attacker: Mega Garchomp with Earthquake or Stone Edge is the plan. Incineroar (53%) stays in reserve for Intimidate and Parting Shot. Watch for Toxapex, which Earthquake answers.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Kingambit fainted, and Palafin used Close Combat, though I'm not entirely sure whether it's in Hero form given the Zero to Hero mechanic timing—but that detail doesn't really affect what happens next.

Now I'm weighing the free switch options: Garchomp at full health versus Incineroar at 53%. Garchomp is the stronger pick since it hits hard and can Mega Evolve later, even though Palafin's Close Combat would do solid damage against it thanks to Garchomp's lower Defense—I'll go with Garchomp.

decisions.thought: 44% SWITCH: dragapult, 23% MOVE: flipturn, 18% MOVE: waterfall

Garchomp (169 Spe) is faster than or equal to Palafin, so it moves first. Palafin (Life Orb, Hero form after switching) is at 90%, and its Close Combat hits hard. Mega Garchomp with Earthquake should pressure Palafin, and Rough Skin punishes its contact moves. Dragapult (Dragon Pulse seen, Atk and SpA lowered) and Toxapex are still unseen threats. Keep Incineroar for Intimidate and Parting Shot when Dragapult or a special attacker switches in. Gholdengo and Chandelure have strong specials.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm checking the matchup now that Palafin switched into Hero form, boosting its stats, and weighing its Water-type Close Combat and typing against Garchomp's Ground/Dragon defenses and speed advantage.

Considering a Mega Garchomp option here—Mega doesn't change its base speed, but boosts Attack and Defense, which could help it tank Palafin's Close Combat while hitting back with a strong neutral Earthquake.

decisions.note: Only one legal action: played without asking.

decisions.thought: 56% MOVE: closecombat, 40% MOVE: waterfall, 3% MOVE: flipturn

Mega Garchomp (full HP, 158 Spe) is active. Opponent Palafin-Hero (Life Orb, Close Combat, about 90% HP) is the main threat, and Garchomp is likely to move first. Earthquake is the best damage on it. Dragapult and Chandelure are down. Still unseen: Gholdengo, Toxapex, Whimsicott. Toxapex is weak to Earthquake. Incineroar (53%) is in reserve for Intimidate and Parting Shot against special attackers like Gholdengo.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Garchomp is at full health and still mega evolved, facing a Palafin-Hero near 90% HP carrying Life Orb Close Combat. I'm checking the type matchup—Fighting against Dragon/Ground is neutral both ways, so Garchomp isn't taking extra damage from that move.

Earthquake against pure Water Palafin is neutral too, and with Garchomp's 222 Attack it should deal roughly 60-70%, not quite enough to KO outright. Dragon Claw and Stone Edge are also just neutral options here, so Earthquake remains the strongest choice, especially since Garchomp should outspeed Palafin.
